  msx-pipeline>⏳ tool: msx-mcp.get_account_overview]
  pipeline-aggregate>⏳ tool: msx-mcp.get_pipeline_summary]
  ai-quota>⏳ tool: msx-mcp.quota_consumption]
  attached-products>⏳ tool: msx-mcp.find_opportunities_by_product]
  workiq-signal>⏳ tool: workiq.ask_work_iq]
  field-playbooks>⏳ tool: sharepoint.findFileOrFolder]
  teams-prior-plays>⏳ tool: teams.SearchTeamsMessages]
  tactical-synth{{\"⏳ think: TACTICAL CONSUMPTION SYNTHESIS for {{inputs.accountName}} (TPID {{inputs.tpid}}). You have 8 source streams in your prompt context. Do the work in this order across your 6 thoughts: (1) From acr-trend, characterize the last 12 months — monthly ACR, MoM delta, identify any decline / plateau / under-pace signal. State the QUANTIFIED gap if one exists; if not, declare 'no shortfall; pivot to gap-creation framing'. (2) From ai-quota, find any model+region where utilization is at or above 80% of allocated quota — that is throttled real demand and a quota-uplift play. (3) From attached-products + msx-pipeline, list every Azure SKU family the customer is already buying — these are the lowest-friction expansion vectors. (4) From workiq-signal, extract every workload reference, every competitor mention, every roadmap signal the customer has uttered in 60 days. (5) Enumerate 5-10 specific expansion candidates as a structured list. For each: workload name, SKU family, estimated $/month at full landing, technical lift required (low/medium/high), 30/60/90 day timing, and a 1-sentence rationale citing which source streams support it. Show the $/month math (units × unit price × utilization assumption). (6) Self-critique: which two candidates are the weakest and why. Return strict JSON.\"}}
  strategic-synth{{\"⏳ think: STRATEGIC CONSUMPTION SYNTHESIS for {{inputs.accountName}} (TPID {{inputs.tpid}}). You have the same 8 source streams. Your job is the offer-shape work, not the math. (1) From workiq-signal + teams-prior-plays, articulate the customer-truth — what does {{inputs.accountName}} actually want right now in their own words. (2) From msx-pipeline + pipeline-aggregate, map the stakeholders: who at the customer holds the wallet, who blocks, who champions; who on Brett's deal team owns each relationship. (3) Without seeing the tactical candidate list yet, declare a strategic frame for this account — is this a workload-migration play, an AI-capacity-unlock play, a FinOps-modernization play, a competitive-displacement play, a renewal-anchored expansion play, or something else. Pick ONE frame; defend it from the source data. (4) Design the offer-shape — incentive structure (MACC depletion accelerator? AzAcc? consumption rebate? engineering sponsorship?), engagement vehicle (POC / sprint / Architecture Design Session / FastTrack), success metric (ACR delta in N days). (5) Name the 3 plays you would prioritize at the strategic frame level (workload categories, not specific SKUs — the tactical-synth quantifies the SKUs). (6) State the single highest-leverage forcing function in the next 30 days that this motion should land against. Return strict JSON.\"}}
  think-tank[\"⏳ wf: think-tank\"]
  email-draft(\"⏳ prompt: Draft an internal email to the {{inputs....\")
  teams-card(\"⏳ prompt: Compose an Adaptive Card JSON payload fo...\")
  plan-render(\"⏳ prompt: Render runtime_inputs.plan_markdown to a...\")
